data.title: Tool Calling
data.tagline: A model’s request for an application to run a named tool with parameters
data.learningOutcome: You can explain that a tool call is a request, not a completed external action.
data.description: A model can request a calendar lookup, but the application must validate the permissions and parameters before it reads the schedule. The returned result, not the request text, proves what happened.

learning.assumes: You have used a chat assistant that can look up calendars, files, or orders.
learning.outcome: You can explain that a tool call is a request, not a completed external action.

explanation.title: Request execution based on tool definitions
explanation.text: Tools are defined with a name, description, and typed parameters. The model fills parameters to request a tool call, but this is only an invocation request—the model does not run the tool directly.

explanation.title: The application validates permissions and parameters
explanation.text: It checks whether the tool is permitted, whether parameters make sense, and whether the user has access.

explanation.title: Real execution results return to the model
explanation.text: Only the executed result from the external tool comes back to the model to formulate the final answer.

data.boundary: Data-shaped parameters are not permission to act. Delete and send actions still need scope checks and confirmation.

lessonPractice.title: An agent says a calendar meeting is created but has not run the calendar tool. What is the accurate state?

options.label: It has only requested a tool call; claim creation only after the app executes it and returns a result
options.feedback: Correct. Choosing a tool is not the same as an external action occurring.

options.label: A meeting title in model text means the meeting exists
options.feedback: Text and real calendar state are different things.

options.label: Tell the user it worked without waiting for the tool response
options.feedback: The tool may fail, be denied, or create a different result; confirm from its real return.

data.agentPrompt: Validate meeting creation with a mock or dedicated test calendar, not a real schedule. Show the proposed time, attendees, and title before the call; simulate one success and one permission denial, reporting only from the actual tool result. Delete any event created in the test calendar afterward.
